main_body: A flat grass ground patch (64x48 px) with a repeating tile pattern of green speckles and clumps; terrain, not a standing object.
top_band: none - uniform green ground texture with no top/front structure; column is mid green #628433 with occasional 1px lighter dots
evidence: Terrain ground patch viewed as a flat surface; the 3/4 top+front contract does not apply to a ground tile. There is no standing volume, no side face, and no elevation drawing. Kind terrain matches. The column scan shows only a uniform green with 1px lighter speckles, as expected for grass ground.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours and a median of 4 colours per tile, against 26 per tile and 80 colours for the reference grass. It has 7% flat-fill coverage where the reference has 0%. The pattern is a small stamp repeated every 16 px in a regular grid, which reads as mechanical tiling, with no tonal variation between tufts. The material has only a base green, one lighter dot, and a darker and a mid clump, so the ramp is shallow compared with the Beodeul grass. It is clearly thinner and flatter than the reference. There are no outlines to judge, since the dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral).
